summary.text: Richard Hricik, a Democratic Charleston-area attorney and former accountant, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of South Carolina to David Stumbo.
He has more than 30 years of civil litigation experience, including before the U.S. Supreme Court.

paragraphs.text: Hricik holds a law degree from William & Mary Law School and a business degree in accounting from Cleveland State University, and he worked as an accountant before practicing law.
He has more than 30 years of experience as a trial and appellate attorney representing clients against corporations in state and federal courts, including the U.S. Supreme Court.
Hricik teaches criminal justice and constitutional law at William & Mary Law School and the Charleston School of Law, and was previously a professor at Charleston Southern University.

Hricik said he would apply the office's power to protect consumers from debt collectors, scammers and insurers, and he took no campaign donations, arguing officials could better serve the public when they are not financially tied to donors.
He ran what he called a no-donation campaign, and he also focused on property rights and making the office more accessible to the public.
He received 47.6% of the vote to David Stumbo's 52.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
